Macrons

Consonantal i

Body, health & movement

sticking plaster noun

also plaster, band-aid

classical

Mart. 2.29.9
Plin. Ep. 6.2.2
Comenius, Orbis pictus 128: Chīrūrgus cūrat vulnera et ulcera splēniīs

splēnium, splēniī n.

noun, second declension

sticking plaster, a patch

Traupman has only taenia adhaesīva, adhesive tape (268), and M-O gives no Latin for plaster, so “band-aid” is our application of splēnium.

Examples

  • Vīsne splēnium? Ecce, jam melius est.

    Do you want a plaster? There, that’s better already.composed

Other words

  • emplastrum, emplastrī n. — medical plaster

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cato; Cels.

See also wound, bandage.

SourcesLewis & Short: splenium · Lewis & Short: emplastrum

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 268.

Comenius from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-comenius).
